prior_findings.evidence: scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:493-528 confines attribution to descendants of the validated lane launcher, but Get-LaneClaudeEvidence accepts any fresh descendant through the subtree tier. A PowerShell profile or a shim that starts an unrelated long-lived process can therefore satisfy the lane after Claude exits or never becomes durable.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:594-625 retains REFUSED lanes in the requested denominator; Get-RunOutcome fails them unless -AllowPartial explicitly produces ACCEPTED-WITH-EXCEPTIONS.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:300-349 validates the session header and bounded tail, and -DeepValidate scans the whole file. Default validation still deliberately cannot detect corruption between the header and final 64 KB, so the original structural-validity concern remains bounded rather than eliminated.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:211-246 applies Windows-native quoting, and Get-WtCommandLine quotes every token except the intentional bare wt separator.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:594-625 reserves VERIFIED for proven == requested, prohibits zero-proven success, and labels permitted incomplete outcomes ACCEPTED-WITH-EXCEPTIONS.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:251-263 rejects duplicate names and comparable paths; the per-run key assigned near line 778 identifies launchers, markers, and result entries.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:632-652 makes Set-Location and marker creation terminating prerequisites, while Test-LaneMarker validates key, runId, cwd, and PID before attribution.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:466-481 rejects name-only classification and requires the resolved command path plus expected arguments for strong attribution.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:573-592 bounds retained run directories and skips live or unreadably claimed directories.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:466-481 no longer accepts an executable merely because it is named claude; the renamed-ping case is rejected.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:370-417 removes timestamp evidence and scans all appended complete records, with foreign sessionId taking precedence. It still promotes a sessionId-less appended record to RESUMED and ultimately VERIFIED, although that write is not attributable to the launched Claude process.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:329-345 requires every examined complete nonblank record to parse and tolerates only an unterminated final record.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:573-592 compares exact process start ticks, treats uncertain ownership as live, and relies additionally on the open active.lock handle to make Windows reject deletion.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:315-328 inspects the byte preceding the bounded window and discards the first decoded line only when the range begins inside a record.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:493-528 now recognizes the normal transient-shim lifecycle, but its subtree fallback proves only that some fresh descendant exists, not that the surviving descendant is Claude or carries the requested arguments.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:389-417 scans every appended complete record before deciding; any foreign nonempty sessionId wins, while expected-session-id and appended-records strengths are reported separately.

scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:270-292 pins the requested range, loops until filled, and returns null on a short read. Callers retry on later polling iterations; ordinary concurrent append does not prevent the pinned range from completing.
scripts/onrestart-launch.ps1:582-588 compares StartTime UTC ticks exactly, and the owner keeps active.lock open for its lifetime.

findings.title: Subtree attribution accepts a non-Claude descendant
findings.detail: When no strong descendant survives, Get-LaneClaudeEvidence returns the first fresh descendant unconditionally. The concrete path is: wt starts pwsh without -NoProfile; the user's PowerShell profile starts a long-lived child such as an agent, watcher, or ping process; the generated launcher then invokes the absolute claude.cmd, which exits quickly or fails after invocation. The profile child remains a descendant of the lane pwsh and satisfies subtree attribution despite not being created by Claude. Independently, an absolute shim may itself start an unrelated helper and exit; absolute-path invocation proves that the file ran, not that every surviving descendant is Claude. Under -Fresh this immediately yields STARTED; in resume mode it can combine with transcript evidence and yield RESUMED.
findings.recommendation: Run the lane launcher with -NoProfile and replace the generic subtree fallback with durable shim resolution or a launcher/shim wrapper that captures the actual runtime PID and executable/entry-script argv. Never accept an arbitrary descendant solely because it is in the launcher subtree.

findings.title: Resume parsing does not handle a record split across the pre-launch boundary
findings.detail: LatestLength may be captured while the final JSONL record is incomplete. Get-ResumeEvidence later begins decoding exactly at that byte, so the completed suffix is parsed as an independent malformed line and ignored. A foreign sessionId contained in that split record is therefore invisible; a later sessionId-less record can produce weak RESUMED. The appended bytes may also be completion of a write begun before launch, so they are not proof that this launch resumed anything.
findings.recommendation: At snapshot time record whether LatestLength is on an LF boundary and preserve the preceding incomplete record or its start offset. During verification reconstruct and parse the split record before evaluating later records. Do not let weak evidence succeed when the boundary was inside a record whose identity cannot be established.

findings.title: Weak transcript evidence is not attributable to the launched process
findings.detail: A complete sessionId-less append is labelled RESUMED even though any concurrent process with access to the transcript could have written it. Combining lane-process ancestry with an independent file mutation does not establish that the attributed process performed the mutation. This retains the central soundness hole from M2, although the evidence string now discloses its weakness.
findings.recommendation: Require an attributable handshake from the launched command or another session-specific signal binding the process to the transcript. If that is unavailable, keep appended-records as UNCONFIRMED rather than RESUMED; only expected-session-id or equivalently strong evidence should prove the lane.

findings.title: Repeated unstable reads can end as UNCONFIRMED
findings.detail: Read-FileRange correctly returns null if a pinned range is truncated before it can be filled, and ordinary concurrent append is harmless. Repeated truncation or replacement throughout the polling window can nevertheless leave the lane permanently UNCONFIRMED. This is a conservative false negative, not a false pass.
findings.recommendation: Optionally distinguish unstable-file retries in diagnostics and re-snapshot only under a defined transcript-rotation protocol.

findings.title: Run lock handle is released only by process termination
findings.detail: The open handle intentionally blocks deletion and allows readers through FileShare.Read. It does not block marker or launcher creation and Windows closes it on process exit, so no soundness defect results. Explicit disposal is absent, making cleanup dependent on process termination and complicating reuse if the script later gains a non-exiting host mode.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the launch/verification body in try/finally and dispose RunLockHandle before the final exit path while preserving lifetime-long ownership.

harness_reason: The eight mutation results materially strengthen the harness and demonstrate that the named regressions make their targeted assertions fail. Remaining gaps are decisive: the K1 positive test uses a synthetic node descendant and never injects an unrelated live descendant from a PowerShell profile or helper-producing shim; resume tests do not place the pre-launch offset inside a JSON record; concurrent append/truncate/replace behavior is not exercised; weak transcript writes are not produced by an unrelated process; lock acquisition failure and handle disposal are not tested; and no end-to-end test executes PATH resolution, wt launch, polling, output, and process exit. Get-RunOutcome is exhaustively tested for two result entries, and the shipped construction maintains one keyed result per selected lane, so no separate unexplained exit-zero route was found. DryRun and ACCEPTED-WITH-EXCEPTIONS exit zero without claiming VERIFIED and therefore are explicit operational outcomes, not false verification.
verdict_reason: The subtree tier can prove an unrelated descendant as Claude, and resume verification can ignore a foreign sessionId split across the launch boundary or accept an unattributed sessionId-less write. Each permits exit 0 with a lane reported as proven without actually verifying the claimed subject, directly violating feature 078. The read-retry and lock-lifetime issues are refinements, not blockers.
